summary: BA spec correctly identifies regex bug, prescribes sound .* -> \S* fix at the right 8 line locations, ACs cover false-positive removal and write/append/commands regressions; Trap 11 wording adequate; minor objections logged as advisory.

1_bug_existence.evidence: Read /root/.claude/hooks/pretool-claude-config-guard.py lines 46-63. _HOOK_PATTERNS lines 47, 48, 52, 53 each contain greedy '.*' between redirect/command tokens and '\.claude/hooks/'. _CMD_PATTERNS lines 56, 57, 61, 62 mirror the same pattern for '\.claude/commands/'. BA's line-number citations are exact.

2_fix_soundness.mental_trace_negative_case: OLD r'>\s*.*\.claude/hooks/' on input 'ls /root/.claude/hooks/foo 2>&1; echo --- ; grep BLOCKED /root/.claude/hooks/bar' -- finds first '>' at '2>&1', '.*' is greedy and traverses '&1; echo --- ; grep BLOCKED /root/' (incl. spaces) up to the second '.claude/hooks/'. Match succeeds -> false positive. NEW r'>\s*\S*\.claude/hooks/' -- '\S*' starts at '&', extends to '&1;' (next char is space), cannot continue across whitespace, cannot reach '.claude/hooks/' (next non-ws chunk requires whitespace traversal). No match -> false positive eliminated.
2_fix_soundness.mental_trace_positive_case: NEW r'>\s*\S*\.claude/hooks/' on input 'echo test > /root/.claude/hooks/evil.py' -- '>' matches, '\s*' eats space, '\S*' matches '/root/' (non-whitespace), then literal '\.claude/hooks/' matches. Match -> still blocks. Same logic applies to '>>' (AC-M4-3) and to commands variant (AC-M4-4). Sandbox script /tmp/regex-validate.py cited by BA confirms this empirically.
2_fix_soundness.edge_cases_considered: Quoted whitespace paths (e.g., '> "/path with space/.claude/hooks/x"') would NOT match new pattern -- BA's Risk 2 acknowledges this acceptable. cp/mv/tee patterns left broad (Won't-Have C1) -- their '.*' between command and path is intentional since cp/mv/tee accept path argument without explicit redirect operator.

3_ac_coverage.ac_m4_1: Read-only false-positive case covered with the exact reproducer the close-report observed.
3_ac_coverage.ac_m4_2: Write-to-hooks regression covered with 'echo test > /root/.claude/hooks/evil.py'. This exercises both line 47 (echo|printf pattern) AND line 52 (bare > pattern) -- either match suffices to block.
3_ac_coverage.ac_m4_3: Append-to-hooks covered with 'cat src.py >> /root/.claude/hooks/foo.py'. Exercises lines 48 and 53.
3_ac_coverage.ac_m4_4: Commands variant covered, plus an explicit read-only-allowed assertion for commands (good -- avoids one-side-only verification).
3_ac_coverage.gap_minor_1: No explicit AC asserts cp/mv/tee patterns (lines 49-51, 58-60) still block since they are NOT being modified. Dev is forbidden from touching them, so risk of regression is near-zero. Acceptable as implicit invariant.
3_ac_coverage.gap_minor_2: AC-M4-2 input form happens to match BOTH line 47 and line 52. If line 47 fix were broken silently, AC-M4-2 might still pass via line 52. Could be tightened by an AC that exercises line 47 specifically (e.g., 'printf %s > /root/.claude/hooks/x'), but acceptable since both lines receive the SAME mechanical substitution.

4_anti_fabrication_trap_specificity.literal_phrase_required: 'independently re-verify' -- yes, M3 mandates this exact substring
4_anti_fabrication_trap_specificity.how_specified: M3 prescribes: 'requires re-running the hook against the exact failing command (or against a synthetic stdin) before the claim is accepted as a reason to skip a downstream step.' This names the verification action concretely (re-run the hook) and the trigger condition (any 'hook X is blocking Y' claim from a subagent).
4_anti_fabrication_trap_specificity.minor_objection: Trap text does not explicitly mandate capturing the exit code and stderr as evidence -- a future fabrication could re-run the hook and silently misreport its output. Recommend dev add 'and record the exit code and stderr verbatim' to the trap wording when implementing M3. Not a blocker; spec is acceptable as written.
4_anti_fabrication_trap_specificity.ac_m1_1_check: AC-M1-1 requires the literal phrase plus the prescriptive instruction. Match for M3.

5_layer_contract_d.novelty: Attempt 1 (R4.2 in spec-20260424-233926.md) CREATED the patterns. Attempt 2 (/redev cycle 1) edited a different file (privilege-guard). This cycle is the FIRST edit to lines 46-63 of pretool-claude-config-guard.py post-creation. File+line intersection with prior cycles = empty. Plus, M3+M4 add a process-trap edit at a different file (spec-20260424-233926.md Section 8) -- two distinct novel actions. Contract D satisfied.

6_dev_time_hint_accuracy.hint_location: BA spec Technical Hints section, line 172
6_dev_time_hint_accuracy.hint_content: 'write the test JSON via the Write tool to a /tmp/ location, then cat /tmp/test.json | python3 /root/.claude/hooks/pretool-claude-config-guard.py. The cat /tmp/test.json command does not match any pattern.'
6_dev_time_hint_accuracy.verification: Confirmed: 'cat /tmp/test.json' has neither '.claude/hooks/' substring nor redirect operator. None of the 14 regex patterns match this string. Dev's own shell will NOT be blocked when running tests this way. Hint is correct and necessary.

objections.issue: AC-M4-2's input matches both line 47 and line 52 patterns. A silent regression in line 47 alone would not be caught.
objections.recommendation: Advisory only. Dev should mentally verify line 47 substitution is mechanically identical to line 52. No spec change required.

objections.issue: Trap 11 wording prescribes re-running the hook but does not mandate capturing exit code + stderr as evidence. A fabrication could re-run silently.
objections.recommendation: Advisory: dev should consider adding 'record exit code and stderr verbatim' to the trap text when authoring it. Not a blocker.

objections.issue: No AC asserts cp/mv/tee patterns (lines 49-51, 58-60) remain functional. Dev is constrained to not touch them, so risk is near-zero, but the invariant is implicit not explicit.
objections.recommendation: Advisory: optional micro-AC running 'cp evil.py /root/.claude/hooks/foo.py' through the post-edit hook to confirm exit 2. Skipping is acceptable.

ba_strengths: Correctly diagnoses greedy '.*' across whitespace as the root cause; '\S*' is the textbook minimal fix.
Constrains dev to EXACTLY 8 lines, prevents scope creep into cp/mv/tee.
Acknowledges Risk 2 (quoted paths with spaces) explicitly rather than glossing over it.
Provides accurate dev-time bypass hint (cat /tmp/test.json | python3 ...) so dev does not deadlock against its own hook.
Trap 11 addresses Mystery 1 (Trap 7 anti-hallucination violation) with prescriptive re-verification, not just process exhortation.
Cycle 2 log entry (M4) ensures spec Section 4 stays current with both the L4 logic fix and the L4 process trap addition.
Conditional S1 (regression test only if tests/ dir exists) avoids creating new infrastructure surface area mid-cycle.
ba_weaknesses_non_blocking: Counts the orchestrator's '5 + 5' as off-by-one without flagging it as worth user confirmation -- could be a misunderstanding rather than off-by-one. Acceptable since the analysis is sound on its own.
M3 trap wording leaves implementation language to dev. A more authoritative BA would supply the exact paragraph for the dev to insert verbatim.
AC-M1-1 does not include a test for the hook re-running command itself -- the trap is process-only, not enforced by automation.
